svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, Segoe UI, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: methyl-flow: how bisulfite reads become a beta table and QC reports
svg.desc: A laptop submits each run to AWS Batch, where a Nextflow head job starts one job per task and every file lives in S3. The pipelines fetch reads from SRA, run nf-core/methylseq, convert its coverage files into the beta table methyl-floor reads, and write QC reports.
svg.text: Dashed boxes are outside AWS. Open the SVG on its own and hover a box for what it does and why.

g.title: Submits runs and deploys the stack. No sequencing data or processing lives here.
One stack, MethylFlowBatchStack, deployed with the CDK (Cloud Development Kit). Billed only while jobs run, plus S3 storage.

a.title: The one command for every run. Uploads config/, pipelines/, and src/ to S3 (Amazon Simple Storage Service) as a run bundle, then submits the Nextflow head process as an AWS Batch job. Pins nf-core/methylseq 4.2.0 and Nextflow 25.04.0.

One YAML (YAML Ain't Markup Language) params file per pipeline and dataset, checked into git, so a run is a file, not a typed command. config/gse95654/runs.tsv pins the 18 SRR (Sequence Read Archive run) accessions.
The AWS CDK (Cloud Development Kit) describes the stack in Python, with tests, and deploys it through CloudFormation in one command.

Runs Nextflow 25.04.0 itself as a Batch job on the on-demand queue, so a Spot reclaim can't kill a whole run and the laptop can close. Copies the run bundle from S3, then submits one Batch job per task.

One EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) instance per batch of tasks, each in a pinned container. Spot capacity is cheaper but can be reclaimed; Nextflow resubmits a reclaimed task up to 3 times. Scales to zero when the queue is empty.
The head job streams each run's progress here when the token secret is set. Lists the QC (quality control) report and tables on the run's Outputs tab (tower.yml).
Holds the Seqera Platform access token. Only the head job's execution role can read it; it is injected as an environment variable, never written to a file.

Every file: downsampled reads and the reference under data/, pipeline output under results/<pipeline>/<run ID>/, Nextflow's intermediate files under work/, and each run's config bundle and log under runs/.
Emails at 80% and 100% of actual spend and 100% of forecast, counting only resources tagged project=methyl-flow.
Creates the VPC (virtual private cloud), compute environments, job queues, head job definition, roles, bucket, secret, and budget from the CDK app.
Console output of the head job and every task, for when a run fails before Nextflow can write its own log.

g.title: Each step reads the last step's output from S3 and writes its own under results/<pipeline>/<run ID>/. Every run also writes Nextflow's interactive execution report and timeline to pipeline_info/.
g.text: Data flow, one scripts/run.sh call per step

a.title: SRA (Sequence Read Archive) study SRP101332: RRBS (reduced representation bisulfite sequencing) of colorectal tumor and adjacent normal tissue from 9 patients.
Human reference genome, primary assembly with no alternate haplotypes. Checked against a pinned MD5 (Message Digest 5) checksum.

Downloads each run with MD5-validated prefetch, rejects SRA Lite files that replace quality scores with a constant, and downsamples to 20 million read pairs with seed 42. Writes the methylseq sample sheet.

FastQC (read quality check), Trim Galore (adapter and quality trimming), Bismark alignment to the bisulfite-converted genome, and Bismark methylation extraction. RRBS mode skips deduplication. Run, not rewritten.
MultiQC (combined quality control) gathers FastQC, trimming, alignment, and methylation reports for every sample into one interactive page.
Reads each sample's Bismark coverage file, keeps chr1 to chr22, chrX, chrY and sites with 10 or more reads, and computes beta = methylated / total reads.

g.title: Reads the beta table and sample sheet. The two files are the contract between the repos; tests/test_convert.py loads them with methyl-floor's own loader.

a.title: Per-sample bisulfite conversion rate, duplicate rate, and coverage; coverage and methylation distributions; PCA (principal component analysis) by tissue and read layout.
Interactive QC (quality control) report: sortable table, then coverage, methylation, and PCA charts with hover. Static PNG versions sit beside it.

DSS (Dispersion Shrinkage for Sequencing data) in R fits a beta-binomial model to methylated and total reads at each CpG (cytosine followed by guanine) site with 5 or more reads in every sample, pairs each tumor with its own patient's normal, and calls DMRs (differentially methylated regions) from FDR (false discovery rate)-significant sites.

DMRs (differentially methylated regions) built from FDR (false discovery rate)-significant sites, a volcano plot, and each DMR's normal and tumor values per patient, as an interactive page and tables.

g.title: What runs before code reaches main.

a.title: Lint and format run before a commit lands.
main is protected: every change arrives as a pull request with passing CI (continuous integration) and is squash-merged.
CI (continuous integration) on every pull request. --locked fails if pyproject.toml and uv.lock disagree.

pytest checks conversion, QC (quality control) math, plots, and both reports on small fixture files; the methyl-floor schema check runs when that repo is installed. r/tests/test_dss.R plants a known DMR in synthetic data and runs in the same DSS container as AWS Batch.

g.title: Data or report: in S3 or the repo
